intervention_names: Drug: Antihyperglycemic medication guideline for management of uncontrolled hyperglycemia presenting to the ED using metformin, sulfonylurea and/or insulin
Behavioral: Diabetes survival skills self-management education
arm_groups.label: Diabetes education and medication management

brief_summary: To demonstrate that a focused Emergency Department (ED) intervention for uncontrolled hyperglycemia enables safe and effective glycemic management and reduces emergency room re-visits. We assessed hypoglycemia BG \< 60mg/dL; change in mean blood glucose and A1C, and ED revisits for hyperglycemia.
brief_title: Stop Emergency Room Visits for Hyperglycemia Project - District of Columbia (DC)

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age \> 18 years
* Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus,
* random BG \> 200 mg/dL,
* willing and able to provide informed consent and to participate in diabetes self-management education (DSME)
* stable for discharge from the ED once hyperglycemia treatment initiated.

Exclusion Criteria:

* type 1 Diabetes Mellitus,
* diabetic ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar non-ketotic state,
* concomitant treatment with glucocorticoids (other than stable maintenance dose therapy),
* cognitive or physical impairment preventing participation in DSME
* unwillingness or inability to provide consent and/or attend follow-up visits.

interventions.name: Antihyperglycemic medication guideline for management of uncontrolled hyperglycemia presenting to the ED using metformin, sulfonylurea and/or insulin

official_title: STEP-DC: Stop Emergency Room Visits for Uncontrolled Hyperglycemia Project in the District of Columbia

primary_outcomes.measure: Total Number of Hypoglycemia Events (Blood Glucose < 60mg/dL) Within 24 Hours of Baseline Visit
